_about: Japan's books (rulings 194, 195 and 196; the Pacific planner's papers 03, 03b and 06): the far side's rows for oil, laid over resources.json and navy.json while the far side's switch is on (src/campaign/far-rows.ts). Kept by hand. Japan keeps stocks as the six powers do. Oil (194): 2 a month at home (Akita's field 1, small wells and plants 1), 34 months in store as the code counts a month on the first day, with the fleet in harbour (about 17 months of the need of a fleet at war), and tanks that hold as much; a lane from America for nine tenths of its need, stopped by war with America and by the freeze (pacific.ts: August 1941 where the stop keeps the book); and the southern oil lane, which carries what the seven oilfields of the south yield to Japan while it holds them (33 to their owners, 19.8 to a conqueror), through the seas between Borneo and Kyushu, less what raiders sink there, and not at all while one of those seas is closed to Japan. Supplies (195 and its rider): Japan's home ground gives 62 in 100 of what its people need ('ratio'), colonies and occupied ground on the far side give nobody anything at home with no ship (resources.ts overTheWater), and five lanes bring shares of Japan's need: Korea 19 in 100 through the Yellow Sea and the Tsushima Strait while Pusan is Japan's, Formosa 5 through the East China Sea while Formosa is Japan's, the rice of Indochina and Siam 8 while no enemy holds Saigon, the rest of the south 9 while no enemy holds Singapore (stopped by the freeze until Singapore is Japan's), and 4 on America's row until the freeze or war. None runs through a sea closed to Japan. The stock is everyone's: 3 months on the first day, room for 6. Terms (196): a computer Japan asks for terms at its month's opening when an enemy holds a twentieth of its home ground by worth and privation has worn all it can off its will to fight ('will.terms', a row by nation, and Japan's is the only row); a player's Japan is spared. America's submarines raid at a quarter of their worth in the far side's seas until September 1943 where the stop keeps the book, and elsewhere until America's twenty-second month at war with Japan (navy.json 'subs').

lanes.name: the American trade
lanes.text: Oil bought in California and shipped across the Pacific, nine tenths of what Japan burns, with cotton, machines and scrap. It ends the day America will sell no more.

lanes.name: the southern oil lane
lanes.text: The oil of Sumatra, Borneo, Java and Burma, by tanker through the South China Sea to the home islands. It is Japan's only while the tankers get home.

lanes.name: the Korea lane
lanes.text: Rice, coal, ore and soybeans from Korea, Manchuria and north China, across the Yellow Sea and the Tsushima Strait. It runs while Pusan is Japan's.

lanes.name: Formosa's lane
lanes.text: Rice and sugar from Formosa, across the East China Sea. It runs while Formosa is Japan's.

lanes.name: the rice lane
lanes.text: The rice of Indochina and Siam, loaded at Saigon and carried north through the South China Sea. An enemy in Saigon stops it.

lanes.name: the southern lane
lanes.text: Rubber, tin, bauxite and ore from Malaya and the Indies, past Singapore and north through the South China Sea. The freeze stops it until Singapore is Japan's.
